page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.u1-c1m2.4xlarge is an x86_64 general purpose instance built on the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by dedicated Intel Xeon processors clocked at 2.5 GHz, delivering 16 vCPUs across 8 physical cores with 2 threads per core. Memory allocation totals 32.0 GB, providing a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Cache resources include 32 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 33 MB shared L3 cache. The CPU exposes AVX and AVX-512F extensions alongside AES acceleration, though advanced matrix and vector instructions like AMX or AVX-512 VNNI are not supported.

The hardware configuration includes no integrated local storage and features zero GPUs. Networking relies on a baseline network bandwidth of 5 Gbps, with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses included. Benchmark results across compute, memory, and application-specific tests consistently position this instance within the average (middle 50%) performance tier. It scores 1,402.0 in Geekbench single-core and 8,470.0 in Geekbench multi-core, alongside a PassMark CPU score of 19,226.97 and a multi-core stress-ng metric of 15,440.75.

Memory throughput reaches 84.73 GB/sec for uncached 256 MB reads and 54.87 GB/sec for uncached writes, complementing cached reads of 831.5 GB/sec. Application testing shows static web serving throughput of 16.69 GB/sec and Redis SET throughput reaching 15.82 million operations per second. Smaller 135M language model inferences execute at 238.95 generation tokens per second, but 7B models drop to 11.38 tokens per second due to the 32 GB memory limit and reliance on CPU-only execution.

Given its 1:2 compute-to-memory balance and absence of local disks, storage must be mounted via network volumes. The instance serves cost-effective general-purpose tasks requiring predictable dedicated compute without large per-core memory demands, including web serving, mid-tier Redis caching, build environments, and enterprise background processing.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.u1-c1m2.4xlarge is an x86_64 general purpose virtual machine featuring 16 dedicated Intel Xeon vCPUs (8 physical cores, 2 threads per core) operating at 2.5 GHz and 32.0 GB of RAM. The instance lacks local storage, requiring network-attached disks, and includes no GPUs. It features a baseline network bandwidth of 5 Gbps. Hardware capabilities include AVX and AVX-512F vector extensions, with a 33 MB L3 cache. Benchmark metrics place the server in the middle 50% across tests, achieving 8,470.0 on Geekbench multi-core, 19,226.97 on PassMark CPU, and 15.82 million operations per second on Redis SET operations. With a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio, this instance is suited for multi-threaded build systems, web serving, background processing, and caching layers with moderate memory requirements.
